analysis: Examined all supplied metadata, patches and source excerpts. These units change documentation only: changelog.d/watchdog-rearm-after-failed-relaunch.md:3 and docs/provider/cli-reference.md:180-185 (head) describe re-arming crash recovery after a drained restart/update relaunch fails, while retaining the drain-timeout fence. No concrete security regression is independently supported by these documentation changes. Relevant boundaries include watchdog rollback authority (T-043/TB-003), connection-bound fresh authorization (T-053/TB-011), and logout credential shutdown (A-008). Integration must inspect ServiceDrain+Recovery.swift (relaunchDrainedProvider), RestartCommand.swift, update activation, LaunchAgent.swift and watchdog state handling: recovery must occur only after confirmed old-process removal, respect provider.auto_restart and lifecycle leases, preserve disabled recovery after drain timeout or persistent stop/logout, and require fresh serving authorization on recovered processes. The supplied base reference documents unconfirmed service removal as failure (:168-178), logout's lifecycle/instance locks (:450-456), and restart freshness requirements (:804-829), but implementation and changed callers are absent. Consequently the claimed runtime behavior and its cross-file safety remain unverified; the selected canonical details do not include the full T-043 definition.
